issue.title: [Feature] Classify looping animations as "status" vs "decorative", and only stop the latter when motion is reduced
issue.body:
## Current behaviour

The global fallback in `app.css`:

```css
/* app.css:3650-3659 */
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  *, *::before, *::after {
    animation-duration: .01ms !important;
    transition-duration: .01ms !important;
  }
}
```

This makes one-shot animations finish instantly, which is correct. But for `animation-iteration-count: infinite` animations the effect is: **each iteration takes .01ms, so it never ends**.

Visually it does look static (one frame finishes the rotation), so **this isn't a visual bug**. The cost is at runtime: those elements' animation timelines never end, so the compositor keeps animations running. Under remote desktop (ToDesk / VNC and friends, which only transfer changed regions), a permanently running timeline keeps marking the region dirty, which can cause refresh anomalies.

Of the 34 `infinite` animations, 12 have no component-level guard and rely only on this global fallback:

| Location | Animation | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `app.css:253` | `spin .9s infinite` | global `.icon.spin` |
| `app.css:618` | `spin .8s infinite` | `.ag-fix.busy` |
| `app.css:2714` | `spin .8s infinite` | sign-in spinner |
| `app.css:3092` | `tdot 1s infinite alternate` | model chip waiting dots |
| `app.css:3944` | `spin .8s infinite` | usage refresh |
| `plugins.css:108` | `spin .7s infinite` | plugin install button |
| `plugins.css:141` | `spin .7s infinite` | plugin main button |
| `library.css:289` | `lib-bob .8s infinite alternate` | bobbing skill icon |
| `library.css:397` | `mk-spin .7s infinite` | marketplace search spinner |
| `library.css:431` | `skeleton-shift 1.4s infinite` | `.mk-desc.wait` |
| `routing.css:257` | `rtlive 1.8s infinite` | live dot for a request in flight |
| `routing.css:735` | `rppulse 1.2s infinite` | replay badge pulse |

## What I'd like

I wouldn't suggest simply adding `animation-iteration-count: 1` — that would freeze every loading indicator, and the user would no longer see "working on it".

Instead, **classify looping animations by purpose** and handle the two classes differently:

### Must keep running (keep `infinite`)

Indicators that carry state — a frozen one loses information:

| Location | Animation | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `app.css:253` | `.icon.spin` | loading state on every icon |
| `app.css:618` | `.ag-fix.busy` | a fix is in progress |
| `app.css:2714` | sign-in spinner | sign-in in progress |
| `app.css:3944` | usage refresh | data is being fetched |
| `library.css:397` | `mk-spin` | marketplace search in progress |
| `routing.css:257` | `rtlive` | a request is in flight |
| `app.css:3880` | `.si-bar i` sweep | indexing progress |
| `plugins.css:108/141` | `spin` | plugin installation in progress |

### Can be stopped (`animation: none` when reduced)

Purely decorative, so stopping it loses nothing:

| Location | Animation | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `library.css:289` | `lib-bob` icon bobbing | pure decoration |
| `routing.css:735` | `rppulse` replay badge pulse | a static style looks the same |
| `app.css:3092` | `tdot` waiting dots | static dots are enough |

## When implementing, please consider

Narrow the global fallback by class instead of taking everything down at once:

```css
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  *, *::before, *::after {
    animation-duration: .01ms !important;
    transition-duration: .01ms !important;
  }
  /* decorative loops: stop them */
  .lib-bob, .rppulse, .tdot { animation: none !important; }
}
```

A more thorough option is to give looping animations semantic classes (`.motion-decor` / `.motion-status`) and stop only the former when motion is reduced. Then a new animation has an obvious convention to follow.

If the in-app switch from #3155 lands, this classification can be reused as the basis for its implementation.

## Another guard that doesn't work

```css
/* routing.css:398-399 */
.rt-livedot.on { animation: rtlive 1.8s infinite; }  /* specificity 0,2,0 */
.rt-livedot { animation: none; }                      /* specificity 0,1,0 */
```

The second is always overridden by the first, so the live status dot keeps pulsing even with the OS setting on. It should be `.rt-livedot.on { animation: none; }`, or the second rule needs higher specificity.

## Expected benefit

- No permanently running animation timelines in reduced mode
- All the necessary state feedback is kept
- A "decoration vs status" convention that new animations can follow

comments.body:
Fixed on `fix/3157-reduced-motion-decorative` (d459527c976d0a1ea06edebd250a384b388cbcff):

- `app.css`: `.mchip .tdot.wait` (tdot loop) now gets `animation: none` under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
- `library.css`: `.lib-icon.busy svg` (lib-bob) stopped the same way.
- `routing.css`: `.rp-tag::before` (rppulse) stopped; and the live dot's existing stop now names `.rt-livedot.on` too — the `.on` rule (specificity 0,2,0) was beating the declared stop (0,1,0), exactly the "another guard that doesn't work" case in this issue.
- Status loops keep animating: the test asserts a waiting request's dot (`.rt-req.wait .to i`) still computes `rtlive` under reduced motion.

Per-selector stops rather than the `!important` keyframe-name block suggested in the issue, because keyframes can't be selected by name in CSS — each looping element needs its own selector.

Test: `internal/gui/tests/reduced-motion-decorative.test.cjs` (Playwright, `reducedMotion: "reduce"` context). Red on the unmodified sheet — computed names were `tdot`, `lib-bob`, `rtlive`, `rppulse` — green after. Chromium on this machine; WebKit can't launch here (host lacks libicu74/libflite1; the existing suite fails identically), so it's unverified on WebKit.

Not done: the semantic `.motion-decor`/`.motion-status` class convention. That's the issue's "more thorough option" and touches every looping rule in the tree — left for a decision on whether the project wants it.
